name: CT-996

lead: CT-996 (tifeglipron) is an experimental oral GLP-1 agonist from Roche for obesity and type 2 diabetes. Fat-loss communities follow it as a non-injectable alternative to semaglutide-type drugs, with lower appetite leading to weight loss and a leaner body.

It is a small molecule taken by mouth, rather than a peptide injection, and small-molecule oral GLP-1 drugs are designed to avoid the injection requirement. Evidence so far consists of clinical trial registrations covering phase 1 and phase 2 studies; published results were not found.

paras: It is not available outside trials. In development it is a pill for people with obesity or type 2 diabetes.
No published safety data were found, and it is not approved.

angle.text: CT-996 is an experimental oral GLP-1 pill that activates the same appetite pathway as semaglutide-type drugs, lowering appetite for weight loss and a leaner body without injections. It has registered phase 2 trials and no published results yet.

lead: CT-996 is an investigational oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist from Roche, also registered under the code RO7795081 and the name tifeglipron.[1][2] Small-molecule oral GLP-1 agonists are a class designed to avoid the injection requirement of peptide drugs.[3]
Published results for CT-996 were not found; the evidence is limited to clinical trial registrations covering phase 1 and phase 2 studies.

paras: A phase 1 study in overweight or obese participants and people with type 2 diabetes enrolled 94 people from 2023.[1] A phase 2 study of daily oral tifeglipron in 352 people with obesity or overweight and a weight-related comorbidity has completed, and a 330-person phase 2 study compares doses with placebo or semaglutide in type 2 diabetes.[2][4] No results were found in the sources reviewed.
